items.english: Outside the door, grown dark, there was the sound of violent rain and wind. A storm.

The family had gathered about the table under the dim electric light hanging by the wall of the narrow room, about to have their supper. Father and mother were both still really young. And the child was a plump, round little girl, just able to stand holding on to the table.

Neither the man nor the woman had yet a single wrinkle in the face. But in the man's hollowed, gentle-looking eyes under his dark brows there showed a drowsy colour of weariness. And in the woman's dark hair and about her slight shoulders there showed a still more sunken deep weariness, and a drowsy restfulness.
The day had ended. The sadness and the suffering of the day were about to flow into the restfulness of the night. And smiling silently, they bent all their eyes upon the child.

Standing unsteadily, with fat, round hands short as balls, the child kept reaching to sweep at the things on the table, leaving not a moment's gap and far too fast. So smiling, they set all the bowls and the teapot and the aluminium pan under the table. On the table there was left only the small spoon the child held and a single small plate.
But the child, giving a noisy cry full of small joy, banged the spoon and the plate down upon the table.
